utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We understand there are some procedural issues to be raised before the next witness. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, thank you for giving us a minute before the hearing. I can indicate that thanks to a clarification we received from the Prosecution yesterday and two of the four matters which were at stake have now been resolved. So there are simply two very short matters which I would like to bring to the Court's attention in relation to this witness, Your Honour. The first concern a couple or perhaps three documents which we may use with this particular witness. We have received these documents, perhaps I should ask to go into private session, Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, good afternoon. The Prosecution calls witness Nazim Bushi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Ms. Regue has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour. We have some binders for Your Honours and for the Defence and the witness, so maybe we can distribute them at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Is your name Nazim Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you a Macedonian citizen of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Have you ever been a member of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: During which time-period you were a member of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I was a member in 2001, from July until the 26th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In which unit did you belong and which rank did you hold within the NLA during this time-period?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I belonged to the NLA unit Brigade 114, brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was your nickname as a member of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: My nickname was Commander Adashi.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you briefly describe your professional background before you joined in the NLA in July 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Before I joined the NLA, I was an officer in the former Yugoslav army from 1987 to 1992. From 1992 to 2001, I was an army officer in the Republic of Macedonia army.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And could you also briefly describe your professional and educational background after you left the NLA in September 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I followed the pedagogical academy, where I graduated in December of 2004.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What about your professional experience after you left the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I was engaged in political activities after the war. We were engaged in the formation of branches. I was in the capacity of assistant coordinator for the formation of the BDI branches in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Within which political party were you working for?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Democratic unit for integration, BDI.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you still a member of this political party?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you holding any official position within this political party right now?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: At the moment, no. I am an ordinary activist like any other party member.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bushi, which was the Albanian representation in the Macedonian public institutions in 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: You mean prior to 2001 or in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Prior to 2001 and even during the crisis of 2001 -- and also during the crisis of 2001.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The Albanians were very little represented in the state and public institutions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the use and the status of the Albanian language in these public institutions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The Albanian language was very -- the use of the Albanian language was very restricted both orally and in writing. We didn't have many opportunities to use it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What about the right to learn in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Until 2001, there was only one faculty, the higher pedagogical school, where teaching was done in Albanian and branch in the Faculty of Theology even though Albanians have always demanded to have possibilities for education in the Albanian language.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: As a result of these facts which was the general feeling among the Albanian population in 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Before coming to 2001, I would have very much liked if you give me the possibility, to give you a presentation of the situation before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please simply explain very briefly to Your Honours which was the general feeling among the Albanian population due to the facts that you have exposed?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The sentiment was very bad from 1990 onwards with the establishment of Albanian political parties and the establishment of a new Macedonian government and state. After the first parliamentary election, with the establishment of independent Macedonian institutions, the Macedonian parliament, the Macedonian government, television, academy and other institutions started to -- Macedonians. After the establishment of the first party, PPD which tried to articulate all the demands of the Albanians through the Macedonian institutions, they fell into deaf ears on the Macedonian government. We felt totally discriminated in all the Macedonian institutions .

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Bushi. Why did you decide to leave the Macedonian army and join the NLA in July 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The main cause was that with the outbreak of the war in Macedonia on the 14th of February, 2001, I personally couldn't remain in an army which had the logo of the Macedonian Republic, when the Macedonian army and police killed my brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi -- sorry, I interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I had something else to add to it. From that time, I had taken medical leave for a long period of time, so on the 9th of June of 2001, a group of policemen, the special intervention unit and some others, many others, came to arrest me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were you released at some point after you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No. I was kept there for two days. Initially they took me to a police station Avtokomanda and then they put a sack over my head. And in two days, I couldn't see anyone, I couldn't recognise anyone, they changed my location three times, they tortured me greatly and finally they just dumped me on -- on the mountain, Vodno mountain, and I was almost -- I had almost fainted.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you learn at some point the reason of your arrest?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The reason they gave me was that I was assisting the NLA during the time I was on medical leave and that they are asking me for -- to tell them the names of some other persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Mr. Bushi, why the NLA was created? Which was the raison d'etre of the creation of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The raison d'etre for the creation of the NLA, dated back from the 1990s to 2001, and the reasons were what I mentioned earlier; namely, the total discrimination of Albanians, something which they could no longer take, until the establishment of a force which was called NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What was the NLA trying to achieve? What were the main goals of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The main goals of the NLA were for the Albanian people to feel equal with the Macedonian people and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, now, you as a brigade commander, I believe you're quite familiar with the structure, the general structure of the NLA. Where were the general headquarters located in 2001? Of the NLA, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The headquarters for the NLA for a brief period was in Prizren. Then it was transferred to Shipkovice.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who was the military leader of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The main leader was Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I'm referring, Mr. Bushi, within the military leadership of the NLA. Who was holding the highest position within the military branch?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: General Gezim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And who else was within the military leadership of the NLA close to Gezim Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: There was Nazmi Beqiri, Dreni, Isa Xhaferi, Isad Demiri, Fatmir Dehari.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to repeat the last names, we couldn't get them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, could you repeat the last names for the record? Interpreters were not able to get them.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Nazmi Beqiri, Commander Iliri; that was a pseudonym. Dreni, Arun Aliu, Zulfi Adili, Fazliu Veliu, Fatmir Dehari, Musa Xhaferi, and many others.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What about the political leader of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The political leader was Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who else was within the political leadership of the NLA close to Ali Ahmeti?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: There were some of the names I mentioned earlier, those were members of the General Staff, and Nazmi Beqiri and Dreni.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. And how many brigades had the NLA in July, August 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: In July of 2001, there was brigade 100 to -- 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16. There was also another brigade which was standing at combat readiness, 111.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was there any plan to create another brigade which was not finally set up?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No. No. There was a special plan in the event of agreement, like the Ohrid agreement being signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, who was issuing orders?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction, in the event -- the agreement not being signed.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: General Gezim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, my question for the -- to have it fully in the record is: Who was issuing orders to the commanders of the Brigade, and the witness answered Gezim Ostreni. And to whom you, as a brigade commander, report within the structure -- the military structure of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: We reported to General Gezim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: How normal person would join the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: It was done on a voluntarily basis, so anyone who so wished could join the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: -- could go with the help of someone he knew, up to the base or the chief of the mobilisation, we call them, of brigade, 114. From that moment onwards, he, after taking the oath, he filled in a mobilisation form filling in his personal data and he -- there was a training centre there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Can I stop you there, Mr. Bushi, for a second. You mentioned that there was a training centre there. Are you talking about the 114th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Where was this training centre located?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: It was located in Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please briefly describe about this training that new recruits would have to follow?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: They underwent military training. They were familiarised with the weapons of 114th Brigade. Then they were informed of international conventions, not to shoot at civilian population, not to kill a -- war hostages and so on, and to now how to administer the first aid, which was given by a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This voluntarily basis that you mentioned as a rule to enter the NLA was also applicable when someone wanted to leave the NLA.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Someone who wanted to leave the NLA should -- could do so upon notification.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, which sort of uniforms were the NLA members wearing?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The NLA members at that time had uniforms of a German make, most of them. For sometime we had Turkish uniforms, but this didn't last for long because they were of a bad quality. Part of the commanding staff had American uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were also uniforms of another colour, different than camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: There were also black uniforms worn by members of the special unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was it mandatory to wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Had these uniforms any sort of insignias, patches on them?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. On the left arm it was the NLA insignia, and in the middle it was the rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Would this rank -- sorry. Would --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours could we please go to 65 ter 778.10. It is tab 11 in your binders. ERN is R062-6967 to 6968. 68.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recognise --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could please --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, these were the NLA ranks. From an ordinary private to general lieutenant. There are others as well. Not all of them are represented in this paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please read aloud the different ranks starting with number 1 to number 6, please.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Lieutenant-general, lieutentant-general major [as interpreted], brigade-general, lieutenant, lieutenant-colonel, and major.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you also please read aloud starting with number 7 until number 11 the different ranks displayed in these insignias.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Captain, Sergeant, Sergeant first class.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. On which basis the different ranks were awarded?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The ranks were assigned on the basis of the military formation in place, and on the basis of the rules of the NLA. As the time went by, these ranks were assigned on merit as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P455, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, how often did you report to your superior, Mr. Gezim Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: We had contacts on a daily basis. The report went in three ways. The first way was by satellite phone; the second through e-mail; and the third by a code that we used for communication between the General and our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the purpose of these communication?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The purpose of this communication was to directly inform the General, Gezim Ostreni, about the situation inside the brigade, the carrying out of the duties that the brigade had during that particular day, and what the plans were for the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please display 65 ter 778.9 it's tab 10 of the binders and the ERN is R062-6933 until 6935. If we could go first to the first page. The next one, please. If we could have an English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you recognise this regulation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. As I said earlier, this is the code of conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you apply this regulation and its content during your daily work?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, up to the last point.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the main purpose of such a regulation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The purpose of the code of communication and the rules of the NLA was for the others not to be aware of the conversations we were having amongst us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this regulation into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P456, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you have personnel meetings with your superiors, meaning Ali Ahmeti and Gezim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The first meeting with General Gezim Ostreni was in Prizren. While the second the second meeting I had was with both of them, Ali Ahmeti and Gezim Ostreni, and it took place in Likov.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which were the purposes of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The purpose of these meetings on the part of the General Gezim Ostreni and the supreme commander Ali Ahmeti was to inform themselves about the brigades, about the needs of the NLA, of the degree of how -- to what extent the rules were respected by the NLA members and the future tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you have meetings with commanders of other brigades?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I only had a meeting with the 113 Brigade commander, Saliu Ukshini [phoen], aka Sokoli, because we were in the same zone while with the other commanders I mainly had contact through phones.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the purpose of such meetings with the commander of the 113th?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The purpose of these meetings was to coordinate things between the two brigades because we shared the area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, in which way the NLA communicated its positions, its calls, to the broader public, to the Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Through communiques.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please display 65 ter 730. It's tab 2 of Your Honour's and my learned colleagues' binders. We see here a communique signed by Ali Ahmeti and dated 11th August 2001 where Ali Ahmeti show the NLA concerned about the coming signature of the Ohrid Agreement which the NLA supported because Macedonia -- Macedonian -- Macedonian government was continuing with repressing activities and also we see that the Ljuboten events are also mentioned. Is this an example of a communique that the -- Ali Ahmeti would issue within the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P457, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please show 65 ter 731. It is tab 3 of the binders. 731, ERN R062-6632. Otherwise we could work in a hard copy if it is not in e-court. It is not in e-court. Your Honours, do you wish me to place the document into the ELMO, as I think that everybody has a hard copy, we could just read them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, you have the document in tab number 5 -- excuse me, tab number 3.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This communique is dated the 14th of August of 2001, also signed by Ali Ahmeti, who is reporting about a meeting held on the 14th of August between the NATO special and himself where an agreement was signed. The agreement envisaged the arrival of the NATO troops and also the NLA demilitarisation. Mr. Bushi, is this another example of a communique that Ali Ahmeti would issue?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P458, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, when you joined the NLA, which was the main task assigned to you by Gezim Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: My main task was to establish the structure of the 114th Brigade, starting from the battalions, and down to companies and platoons, and this was to be carried out pursuant to the rules of the NLA, military rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please explain us a bit more about these battalions, companies, and platoons. Could you please explain us how many did you have and who were the commanders?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The 114th Brigade had two battalions, the 1st and the 2nd Battalion. The commander of the 1st Battalion was Sahid Ahemiti, aka Commander Kabashi, the commander of the 2nd Battalion was Ilir Tahir Sylaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which other structure -- which other unit were below the battalions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: There were military units known as companies, platoons, and squads.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did -- had the 114th Brigade any special unit within its structure?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: There were two special units which were directly under my command, the special unit known as Arusha, and the other unit called Teli.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Arusha and Teli are individuals, are persons?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Arusha and Teli were also persons, but the units were also named after them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, that the second unit Teli is a special reconnaissance sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please state the name of the commanders of the two units and also which were the main tasks of these units?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Nazmi Sulejmani aka Arusha and Lefter Gaxhaj, aka Teli. The task of the first special unit known Arusha was rapid intervention within the framework of the brigade in the front lines, while the task of the second special unit, the sabotage reconnaissance unit, was to go outside the border of the front line and collect information.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Where was the headquarters of your brigade located?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The 114th Brigade headquarters was situated in the village of Nikustak, Kumanovo area.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: How many people were in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: About one thousand.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you also name the staff of your brigade and the positions that they were holding?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. The commander of the brigade was Nazim Bushi known as commander Adashi. Deputy commander was Halil Paloshi, S-1 Ragmi Emini, aka Musteqja was chief of personnel and mobilisation issues. S-2, Baki Mustafa, intelligence and counterintelligence officer. Ramadan Limaj, known as commander Kitra, chief of operations. Xhavit Hasani, officer for morale and information. Selam Hasani, chief of logistics. Amzi Amziju, communications and my personal secretary. Commander of the police, Jahi Nuju. And the head of the military hospital, Rivdan Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who if any of your subordinates was authorised to issue orders on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Only Halil Paloshi had this authorisation to issue orders in my behalf, but I would like to stress here, only in my absence. If I'm not present.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did every exercise this authorisation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which type of weaponry had your brigade back in July/August 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The 114th Brigade in early July and late August 2001, had the following light and heavy weapons starting from pistols, then automatic rifles, Kalashnikovs or known as AK 47, sniper rifles, hand-held mortars, 150 and 500 type, Gulinovs, 12.7-millimetre launchers, cannons, OSA, and mortars of 62 millimetres and 82 millimetres respectively.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks Mr. Bushi. Could we please show 65 ter 284. In particular, within the range N001-8730-N001-8763. If we could please go to the page number 7 both in English and in Macedonian. And in the meantime could we go briefly into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This is not the page. Actually it is page number 7 within the range. I think that you are looking at the wrong range in the 8725 but we should look at 8730. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, if we could look -- the last paragraph of the English version and the second paragraph, starting from the bottom of the Macedonian version. We can read, Mr. Bushi, that the 114th Brigade is said to have received the order to close the existing gap north of Skopje between Radusa and Tanusevci, and these would form it possible fighting in the whole area of the 111th, 113th, and 114th brigade, NLA brigades. And the Blace border crossing would be in the sphere of influence of the NLA. Mr. Bushi, did you ever carry out this assignment?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, we did not. This was an option to be executed in case the Ohrid Agreement failed to be signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We can remove the document from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, had the NLA internal relations dealing with a broad range of issues?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, there was an internal rules of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For the record I see that my question has not been recorded. I just asked whether the NLA had internal regulations. Could we please call 65 ter 778.1. It's tab 7. The ERN should be R062-6654. And if we could go to the page number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We see here a regulation which needs National Liberation Army, General Staff. Personnel and material formation of the brigade. It's approved by Ali Ahmeti and signed by Gezim Ostreni. Could we please go to the second page. Mr. Bushi, are you familiar with this regulation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. It is the regulation that I mentioned earlier on the formation of brigades and other formations.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In this chart we can see, first start from the left sides, positions according to their formation, then we see first name and last name, which has to be filled, date of birth, then we have the ranks, different positions as general high-ranking officer, officer, we also have indicated here the uniforms and also the weapons. Which was the purpose of this chart, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: This was filled by the -- by the officer of mobilisation, Ragmi Emini. The aim was to keep data and when inspection came anyone who came from the General Staff, such documents and data were shown to him or them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this regulation into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P459, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply to give an indication to that we will not object to any of these so-called regulations of the NLA. However, we would make the point that this should not be interpreted as an agreement on our part that these documents are otherwise reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to tab number 8, 65 ter 778.2 the ERN is R062-663, if we can go first to the page number 1. We can read in this regulation also NLA, General Staff, personnel and material formation of the infantry battalion also approved by Ali Ahmeti and dated 2001. If we could go, please, to the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We see here again a chart, Mr. Bushi. Well, first of all let me ask you, are you familiar with this regulation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, I am. This is a regulation on the establishment of battalions. As I said, this was filled by the mobilisation officer and the purpose is to have some proof to show during inspection by the General Staff or the staff of Brigade 114 as a proof to show our respect for the rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Once these charts had been filled, did you supervise the work of your subordinate who filled them?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Sometimes, yes; but this was the duty of this officer that I mentioned, and it was inspected by Ramadan Limaj, who was the chief of operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Again, we see a chart with the unit and different units mentioned. And then we see a number, a name of unit and venue. What venue, exactly? What had to be filled in this place, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I'm not very clear about what are you putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Excuse me, if we look at on the upper part of the document, on the third square starting from the left, at least the English translation says venue. I was asking what had to be filled within this.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I can't see it, or maybe you are referring to some other chart or ... I can't see it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you have a chart with the title "Mobilisation plan of the Infantry Battalion"?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you read in the upper part, do you read "1st Unit" in the first square?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe with the assistance of the usher if you can look at the hard copy. Excuse me, it's tab number 8.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I would kindly ask to you indicate again to me where do you want me to see?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you look to the upper part, we see "unit," and then below we see "infantry battalion," "deputy commander,""battalion command," and then if you look on the right side you see -- you can read number which has the name of the unit which has to be filled. In the second -- it's actually the third column, Mr. Bushi, you have to look at the third column. The third column.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I think there is something which is not clear, either due to interpretation or I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: If it's possible, someone to help me.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can be of some assistance it, seems like the Macedonian translation says something different. And I'm trusting my more able neighbours, it seems to say at that it refers to a place for the plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you able to assist us, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Now I'm clear. That is the venue for plenification word for word. It indicates the operation zone for the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: , Your Honours, I'll will seek to tender this regulation into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We would be grateful if my learned colleague could clarify what battalion and what brigade those charts are supposed to refer to. We are not clear whether the Prosecution is suggesting that those are brigades and battalions which relate to the 114th or what exactly they refer. We are unclear about that. I'd be grateful if that can be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi -- well, first of all, did you apply this regulation to your brigades and to your battalions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, in general, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And can you -- do you have knowledge if this regulations were applied to other brigades and to other battalions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: They were applied to all brigades and battalions. It was a law, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Can we please look at tab number 1 -- excuse me, number 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P460, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, now it's 65 ter 778.3, tab number 9. If we could go to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We can see -- we can read "regulation on the competencies and work of the brigade command" also approved by Ali Ahmeti and signed by Gezim Ostreni in 2001. Are you familiar with this regulation, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it personally, I and other brigade commanders. Could we please move to page number 2 in both Macedonian and English. In this table of contents that you are going to see now in the Macedonian language on the right screen, we can see different positions brigade command-- excuse me, commander of the brigade, legal advisor, head of the officer for information and public relations, liaison officer, et cetera. Did you have in your brigade, in your 114th, these positions.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, we had. We had the officer responsible for morale and formation, Xhavit Hasani. The chief of personnel or mobilisation, Emini, Ramadan Limaj for operations for logistics, Selam Hasani --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now if we could go please to page number 4 of both English and Macedonian. We see in the second paragraph that it reads "that the aim of these regulations is to define the duties and responsibilities and rights of officers and other staff members at the brigade command so that they can carry out their functions and duties." Was this the aim of this regulation, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go now to page number 6. Here we see a title which reads: "Commander of the brigade." Now it will appear on the right side of your screen, Mr. Bushi. If we read in item number 1 of this page which starts with the commander of the brigade, it says: "He is to run and command all brigade staff in peacetime in a states of emergency and in war. He is to carry out his duties in accordance with the laws, with internal regulations with the UCK and with instructions from the UCK commander. Was this one of your main obligations as brigade commander, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, I had many tasks. This one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, if we look actually at item number 7, it says that he is to ensure and insist that all the staff members of the brigade command and their subordinates carry out their duties and obligations according to a work plan. Did you prepare, did you draft such a work plan, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, we did. That was the responsibility of the chief of operations, with his three assistants. They drafted the plans and I approved them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we look at item 11 it reads: "He is to direct planning for military readiness mobilisation and for the use of the brigade command and subordinate formations and is to approve the plans in question." Mr. Bushi, does this rule mean that any military operation to be carried out within your brigade had to be approved by you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. If we read item 13, it says at a certain time every day he is to report to the UCK commander about the general situation in the brigade. Does this rule refers to your daily reporting with Gezim Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, if we look at item 14 it says, the last three lines: "At a certain time every morning, he is to receive a report by phone or other oral communications from the commanders of subordinate units and close staff of the command," I think that we are have to move to the other page, "on the general situation in their brigade." Did you receive such reports from your battalion commanders and unit commanders on daily basis?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, in order to be able to coordinate and to have an overview of all tasks, the staff of the brigade held meetings every evening at 2100 hours, where the battalion commanders as other unit commanders as well as representatives from the brigade staff participated.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, Mr. Bushi, this regulation did apply to the other brigades of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this regulation into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P461, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please display 65 ter 384. It is the tab -- the map displayed it -- it is in tab 5 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, you can also look at tab 5 of your binder where you have a hard copy of the map. If we can zoom to the coordinates 41, 42, and verticals 59, 58. If we could place these coordinates in the centre of the screen. And in the meantime, Mr. Bushi, which was the area under the responsibility of the 114th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The AOR of the 113th brigade?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Explain this to us?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No problem, I will not mark anything. I understand. The border starts between Vistica and Matejce. And then Vistica, Nakustak linking to a place called Bara.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you talking about the operational area or the zone of responsibility of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Now I'm talking about the operational area, not the area of responsibility. So Vistica, Nagustak, Bara, Dzafa, there is a line here which is not marked on the map. We had an observation post here while the opposite side was covered by 113 brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you able to see the operational area also in the map displayed on the screen, Mr. Bushi. It's exactly the same map. If you are able to see the locations, we will use the map in the screen.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Poorly. I can see it poorly. Vistica, Nagustak, Bara, Dzafa, in this direction, up to the Matejce Monastery.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe if we could have the assistance of the usher to give him the -- with a pen.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please take the electronic pen that you're going to be given and draw a circle in the operational area of the 114th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: While in Mojanci and Orlance villages, we only had observers. This goes also for Aracinovo after the NLA withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you able to mark with a cross and then write a number in the observation post that the NLA had in the electronic map?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, just let me have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And which observation post is this one?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Mojance.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write number 1 next to the cross?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see any other observation post?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, Orlance.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write number 2.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see any other observation posts of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: And we had one in side the village of Haracin.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write number 3.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: These were the three observations posts that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please draw a line indicating the front line of the 114th Brigade and indicate from which location to which location the front line was running?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The front line stretched from Nagustak to Vistica, Matejce, Bara.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please draw a line or that includes the circle that you already ...

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the borderline of the operational area of 114th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So the circle that you drawed, it's actually also the front line of the 114th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Are you -- could you indicated also the headquarters of your brigade in Nagustak, as you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write number 4.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Where were the headquarters of the 1st Battalion located?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion staff was in Nagustak village and it also included Vistica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So it was in the same location that you had the headquarters of your brigade, or it was in a different location?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, it was in a different location.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please indicate that and write number 5?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So the small line that you drew on the right side of the cross, that's the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: It's near the cross where the number 5 is. It's inside the village of Nagustak, but a different location, within the same village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What about the headquarters of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The headquarters of the 2nd Battalion was in monastery of Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please indicate it and write number 6 next to it?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now are you able to see, Mr. Bushi, in this map, army positions that the Macedonian army had in 2005 -- excuse me 2001, in August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if he could use a pen of a different colour. Is that possible or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the positions was at Ljubotenski Bacila.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please write number 7.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see any other army position, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: There are several other positions in the eastern part, above Ljuboten village. This was a sort of bare front line. I don't know the exact locations now on the map, but I can show you approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you could please draw a line where you think that the front line of the Macedonian army was above Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I will try to find it using the map before me. I can see Ljubanci on the printed map that I have, but I will try to find it on the screen. It should be somewhere here, Ljubanci. And it is one of the positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you write number 8 next to this position?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see any other position? Or if you don't see it, you can just state the name so we have the names of the positions in the record, if you are not able to see them in the map.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: There was one at Ravno.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: There was one in Ravno?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Ramno. And at Kodra Fudra.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are they located in this area and you cannot see them, or are they outside of this map?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No. You can see Ramno. It's here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, could you please write number 9?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before we go further, Ms. Regue, the witness says he's having difficulty reading on the screen, and I can well understand that. It seems very evident that he has marked as number 8 not what he thought he was marking. He was looking for Ljubanci, as I understand it. And that is a little to the north and to the west of the position that he has marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, If could you please draw an arrow from number 8 to Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Actually, Ljubanci is a bit up north from where you indicated in the screen, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Another two to three centimetres on the screen north-west.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a dot here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay, thanks Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And I think we've reached our time. Are you wanting more marks on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you see any other army position, Mr. Bushi, on this map? If you don't see them, you can say them on the record.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: There are positions on the eastern part as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay, can you say simply the names.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Rastak and the front line connecting with Ljubanci and Ljubotenski Bacila.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you'd better have those marked, if you want them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you able to see them, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Here is Rastak.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please write number 10.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: And with the interrupted line, I will mark the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P462, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume, then, at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, before you indicated in the map the area -- the operational area of your -- of your brigade, of the 114th Brigade --?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And he's not going need to mark anything else, Mr. Usher, so that's okay. Thanks for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now which was the zone of responsibility, not the operational area, the zone of responsibility of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The area of responsibility was Skopje and its outskirts.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what is the difference between the zone of responsibility and the operational area.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The operational zone includes the moment -- the moment when you are supposed to operate, to act, when you have an order, and the other one is the area that you are responsible to cover in case of an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please go to tab number 4 which is ERN N006-7991.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what do you see in -- in the screen?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was Ljuboten within that zone of responsibility of the 114th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. But not the area of operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which battalion of your brigade was responsible for Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: It was the 2nd Battalion and, if need be, also the units of special intervention.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the closest headquarters of your brigade with -- to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Our headquarters was in Matejce, the 2nd Battalion, and there was a position 2, 300 metres outside the monastery.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which was the name --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Pal Langro [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. How far away were these positions and the headquarters of the 2nd Battalion with regard to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: As the crow flies, about five kilometres. If you walk, it takes you seven to eight kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you able to see the monastery headquarters or the observation point in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, are you not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we see at the hills in the background, could you simply describe where it's located?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. You cannot see it very well. But I can show the direction in which it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If you could please take the pen that the usher is going to give you, and if could you mark in the screen with an arrow the direction where the monastery was located and the observation point was located.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: You cannot see the observation point from here. It is only the direction from the monastery.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. With this arrow you indicated the direction of the monastery and the observation point or only the monastery?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Only the direction towards the monastery, but not the observation point. You cannot see it from here.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. It is not depicted. And how far was the observation point from the monastery?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: One, up to one and a half kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we look at the hill, it should be towards the eastern part of the hills or towards the western part of the hills?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Towards the eastern part.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I will seek to tender this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P463, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just as a matter of clarification, when you are referring to the monastery, are you referring to the monastery of Matejce that you mentioned before, when we were looking at the other map?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks. Mr. Bushi, which was the importance, if any, that Ljuboten had for the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: It didn't have any importance for the NLA, because we could resort to Haracin village for any needs we had, particularly logistical needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: What about as a base to obtain weapons for your brigade. Was Ljuboten used for this purpose?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No. For us it was Haracin village which was of major importance.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was Ljuboten used as a recruitment centre for new members of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you aware if some members of your brigade were originally from Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You don't recall any name of any member of your brigade which was from Ljuboten, or you are not aware that there was any person from Ljuboten who was a member of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I remember some names from Ljuboten, like Riza, Marsori, Sherafadini, Islami, and some others who, if I know, if I see, I would certainly recognise. They were members of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Okay. So there were actually villagers from Ljuboten who were members of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And approximately, if you can recall, how many?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I would say about ten, 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are we talking in July/August 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, where were you the weekend from Friday, 10th of August, 2001 to Sunday, 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I was in Nagustak village, at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you learn at some point on Friday, the 10th of August, about the Ljubotenski Bacila incident, meaning eight Macedonian soldiers were killed because of a mine?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. I heard through the media and through some phone calls I had with Mr. Baki.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please state the family name of Mr. Baki?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Baki Halimi.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was Baki Halimi a member of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, he was not. I used to know him from the past.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was he assisting in any way the NLA, with regards to logistics, weapons?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was he also called Lisi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Was he also called Commander Lisi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No. I don't know. Why should he called a commander when he was never a NLA member.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: On that Friday, did you receive any order, did your brigade receive any order, to plant the mine in Ljubotenski Bacila?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you order to plant the mine in Ljubotenski Bacila to any of your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't give any orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, any of your soldiers from your brigade plant the mine?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, it cannot be.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bushi, you testified that you stayed in the headquarters of your brigade during all the weekend. Also, at some point on Saturday or Sunday, 11th, 12th of August, did you learn about the events in Ljuboten, about what was happening in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who told you, who informed you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Baki informed me, Baki Halimi.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: When did he inform you and how?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: He called me on the 10th and 11th and 12th, the time during which the Macedonian forces, police and army forces, undertook the attack against Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: At some point during that weekend, or later on, did you find out that some people had been killed in Ljuboten during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. I learned that some people were killed, but I didn't know any of the deceased.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So at some point, taking your question [sic], I assume that you learned about the names of the deceased?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: During later times, I learned that one of them, Rami Jusufi, was a former classmate of mine. But I saw the names written on the grave stones.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge were these people members of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And Mr. Bushi, during the weekend 10 to 12 August, 2001, did you order to open fire towards the army positions around Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you order to open fire against the police positions in the Orthodox church in Ljuboten during the same weekend, 10 to 12 August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you send any member of your brigade to Ljuboten that weekend, 10 to 12 August?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now, if we could please look at tab 6 which is 65 ter 284 within the range N001-8764 to 8780. If we could please look first at page number 1, which will be the cover. We can see in this document, this document contains the names of members of the NLA in Macedonia as well as NLA Macedonian contacts during the period from April to October 2001. And now if we could go to page 2 in both English and Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We see in the third line your name, your nickname, Adashi, and then Bushi Nazim, 114th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if we could please scroll a little bit more to the right, so we can see the main text. Thanks. Maybe if we could zoom it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: It reads next to your name, Mr. Bushi: "Presume commander of the 114th Brigade in the area of Nagustak Ljuboten on 10th August 2001 reported that the village of Ljuboten had been encircled by Macedonian Armed Forces, was told by Gezim Ostreni not to do anything in order to avoid a massacre of the population. Demanded -- demanded EU observers for Ljuboten."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Now if we could go, please, to page number 11, also both in English and in Macedonian. On the left side in the first row we see the name Gezim Ostreni, and if we could now move to the text to the right side. Thank you. We see on the third line -- excuse me, in the first line. "Advise the commander of the 114th Brigade on 10 August 2001 not to do anything near the village of Ljuboten so that the Macedonian Armed Forces would not be able to use the presence of the KLA to justify a massacre of the civilian population. Wanted to send EU observers to Ljuboten."

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, did you receive an order from Ostreni not to go, not to do anything in Ljuboten on the 10th of August? You are not able to receive translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He is still receiving.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He ordered me not to undertake anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you comply with his order?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you also discuss with him the possibility of calling international observers or members of the government?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, we discussed this. I had a contact on that day with the deputy prime minister Xhemal Musliu, I asked him to call on the phone of the minister of the interior, Ljube Boskoski, or the minister of defence, Vlado Buckovski, regarding the situation in Ljuboten. And he said to me that I cannot reach them, they are not answering their phones. And we contacted the representatives of the international community and asked them to go to Ljuboten and see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which international organisation are you referring? Which international organisation did you contact?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The European Union representatives and OSCE and International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did any member of your brigade approach you or approach any of your subordinates to ask for permission to go to Ljuboten during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. One of them had come to Nagustak - I don't know his name - he asked Ramadan Limaj, the chief of operations, for an approval to go to Ljuboten. I received that message and I turned it down, his request, and I said that nobody should go to Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, any member of your brigade went to Ljuboten that weekend.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Who was Xhezair Shaqiri?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Xhezair Shaqiri was the NLA commander responsible for the village of Haracin. He was not a member of 114th Brigade. He was a member of the 113rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you see him during the weekend 10 to 12 August, 2001, in your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you have any discussion with him that weekend?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes. There was a short discussion, viewing the possibilities, how to help Ljuboten, and I said to him that we have an order from the General Staff not to undertake anything at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: So just to be clear, did you issue to him any order to go to Ljuboten that weekend, 10 to 12 August?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could he have left the headquarters and going to Ljuboten without you knowing?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I don't think he went to Ljuboten, but he was not my subordinate. He was not under my command.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But he could have left the headquarters without you knowing.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: It could have been possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Suad Saliu?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: If I see him, maybe I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Does the name sound familiar, as a member of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you order to a person with this name to go to Ljuboten that weekend, 10 to 12 August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't order anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: You just -- you testified before that Xhavit Hasani was your chief of morale and operations. Where was Xhavit Hasani during the weekend 10 to 12 August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: He was with me at the headquarters in Nagustak village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did he ever leave the headquarters during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Where were your immediate subordinates meaning Paloshi and Ramadan Limaj during that weekend, 10 to 12 August?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Halil Paloshi, the deputy commander, was in the monastery of Matejce, while Ramadan Limaj was mobile. He was moving in Nagustak. He was a sort of chief of operations and he was visiting the points.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Which points, if you have the knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: He was touring the positions at Vaksince and Nagustak. I think he toured all the positions up to the monastery.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did your brigade come under fire from Macedonian positions during the weekend 10 to 12 August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Our brigade was constantly under attack but the attacks were more intense on the 10th and 12th, from the direction of Rastak and Ljubanci, and from the other side from the direction of Umindol, Ropalce and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the last name of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of the last village that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Romanovce, Umindol, and Ropalce.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you respond to these attacks?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: We responded only to the attacks coming from the direction of Umindol, Ropalce and Romanovce, but we did not respond to the attacks coming from the direction of Rastak.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And what about the attacks coming from the direction of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No. We did not respond to these attacks either because they were far from us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was any personnel casualty in your brigade during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, according to the information I had, on the 12th we had one person killed and one injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you remember where these two people were killed and injured?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: On the 11th, Musafer Agushi aka Muski was killed while Bejtullah Ademi was injured. Both of them were killed and injured in Nagustak village through a hand-held rocket launcher attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just to clarify, which day was that that they were injured and killed? The 11th or the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: On the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if you know, from which attacks they were injured and killed from the ones coming from this three positions, Ropalce, Umindol, and Romanov or the attacks coming from Ljubanci and Rastak?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: I think it is the Romanovce and Umindol villages but concretely from which one, I don't know because there was attack coming from all three sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please just see on the screen Exhibit P462 again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is the map that you just marked. Just to be clear, can you see in this map the three positions that you mentioned now, Ropalce, Umindol and Romanovce?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, they cannot be seen here. They are opposite Vistica and Nagustak.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Would that be facing your front line on the eastern part of your front line?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: We can remove the exhibit. Could we go please to tab 14 which is Exhibit 1D160.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise to my colleague. We would simply like to place on the record that at this stage the Prosecutor has been eliciting evidence from this witness which is directly contradictory to the evidence of another Prosecution witness and who was not in any way challenged on the evidence that he gave. We note that for the transcript. We will take this matter in cross-examination but we wish to point for the record that this is being done at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Mr. Mettraux, I'm sure that you will deal with this issue in cross-examination. Could we please see 1D60, page 1 in English and in Macedonian, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is a document coming from the UBK dated 14th of August, 2001. And as we see the title reads: Assessment of the high level of the violated security situation in Ljuboten village and the surroundings? If we could please now go to the second page. If we read in the third paragraph we see that Ljuboten is mentioned as the main logistic base of the NLA, also a place for procurement and storage of weapons and mobilisation of new volunteers. Mr. Bushi, were you using Ljuboten for these purposes, was the NLA using Ljuboten for these purposes?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: The NLA did not use the village of Ljuboten for any of these listed purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please. We see it is the fourth paragraph in both languages. Where it reads that on 12th of August 2001 with regards to the situation in Ljuboten village, Gezim Ostreni informed Fazil Valiu that the villagers should stay in the basement and NLA members should go out and respond to the Macedonian security forces. Mr. Bushi, first of all, who was Fazil Valiu.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Fazil Valiu was a member of the General Staff. He had no such competence to order Gezim Ostreni such a thing and definitely there was no NLA presence in Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, the document only reads that Ostreni informed Fazil Valiu so it is the other way around, no?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: That could be possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: But in your daily communications with Ostreni, would you have learned about such an order, meaning that the NLA members will go out and respond to the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise to barge in the question, but I think the witness should be asked first and foremost whether he is aware of this communication between these two persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: I was going to find that out about the daily communications that this witness has had with Gezim Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Were you aware through your daily communications with Gezim Ostreni about this communication between Fazil Valiu and Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Considering that Ljuboten was within your zone of responsibility, would you have been informed, if such order would have been issued?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Considering that Ljuboten was within the zone of responsibility of the 114th Brigade, if an order would have been issued that NLA members will go to Ljuboten and will respond to the Macedonian security forces, would you have learned about such an order?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And if we look at the paragraph number -- well, paragraph 5, we see your name that a member of the so-called NLA [indiscernible] in the ongoing situation he address an issue to Nazim Bushi, the commander Adashi, asking whether there are conditions to act against the Macedonian security forces. Nazim Bushi inform him that they can operate in villages Brodec and Ljuboten and that in order to start actions, he can deploy the troops of a special unit and one more unit in only an hour and a half." Did you have such exchange with a person about this matter?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Did you issue an order to start actions and deploy your troops, the brigade troops?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI
utterances.text: No. I did not give any orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks.
